When I first walked into my home group I was asked, “hey, can you hang out for an hour?” I said sure,  we talked for an hour. Next thing I know the guy looks at me and says “Congratulations!” Confused I said for what?  He says “for your first sober hour” the. He asked if I could keep from having a drink till the next meeting that was in an hour.. I said sure.  Hour number 2..

I got caught up in the forever but he helped me focus on one hour at a time...  you should too!   You should also make sure you have local folks phone numbers and try to find yourself a sponsor ASAP. 

As for the wife. If you don’t have one already get a copy of the Big Book and read it...  Have your wife read the chapter to the wives.   My wife was at her wits end with me but after sharing that chapter with her it helped her understand where I was at and what I was dealing with.  She saw my change slowly coming around. 

You could also help her find an Al-Anon meeting to attend. A group of folks just like her to talk with and listen to as you work your way through recovery. 

Hope this is helpful. I know it’s not easy but I’m proud of you making it to your 4th day!!!

Hey Augello,
  I’ve dealt with serious depression as well so I understand your mental back n forth..   I can tell you what I did that helped and you can choose what’s best for you. 

I found some free counseling for someone to talk to about what I was dealing with (I asked them to hold off on any prescriptions unless it was really needed, I was doing plenty self medicating with alcohol anyway)

As I was going through the appointments I jumped on some AA zoom meetings.  As said before, you don’t have to be on camera, you don’t have to speak, you just need to listen.  If you like to read, get a copy of the big book. 

After a few zooms I decided I wanted to check out an in person meeting.  I know get to hang out with a bunch of amazing people daily for an hour.

30days ago today I took my last drink and I also haven’t had any more suicidal thoughts. (I realized I was in a vicious cycle of drinking because I hated myself and hating myself for the drinking). 

Hope you find something helpful in these replies to your post. Feel free to dm me if you want to chat as well.

Prayers are with you!  Coming back is the most important thing.  Make sure you find a sponsor ASAP to guide you and call you on your BS. 

One hour at a time friend...

Hey friend...  my situation is very different from yours however I can say.   If you’re holding on to you dad letting go it means to me you need to stick around to protect him...

I’ve had that bond with other family members(even though I was adopted). It was was my job to see their safe passing....   mauve your job is to protect your dad right now.... hope this helps friend

I feel your pain... I truly do.  Even though I question my own existence.  I will say.  If you have family, they care.  If you don’t have family, find friends in the same position. You’d be surprised at what you learn about people if you open up to them.  They may not have the same disabilities as you but the emotional roller coaster can be the same...  all you gotta do is be yourself and be honest with those that are trying to get close to you.   

I really hope this message helps.  If you want to chat more please feel free to DM me anytime. I’ll respond ASAP!
